title: The Biggest Classroom in the World
intro: You are going to read about a girl in Australia who goes to school without leaving her home.

passage: Ten-year-old Ellie Morgan lives on a cattle farm in a remote part of central Australia. The nearest town is 400 kilometres away, and there is no school near her home. So every morning at eight o'clock, Ellie walks across the garden to a small room, turns on her computer and says, “Good morning, Mrs Baker!” Ellie is a student at the School of the Air.

The School of the Air started in Alice Springs in 1951. At first, teachers and children talked to each other by radio. Children had to press a button before they spoke, and the sound was often bad. Today, students use the internet. They can see their teacher and every classmate on the screen, but some of these classmates live more than 1,000 kilometres away.

Each online lesson lasts about thirty minutes. After that, Ellie does her schoolwork on her own. Her mother helps her, and some families have a governess, a young woman who lives on the farm and teaches the children. “It's hard to concentrate when you can hear the cows outside,” Ellie says, “but I like working at my own speed.”

Of course, students at the School of the Air miss some things. They can't play football with friends at break time or chat in the corridor. That's why the school organises special weeks. A few times a year, families drive for many hours to Alice Springs. The children finally meet their classmates face to face, play sports and go on trips together.

Some people worry that these children feel lonely. But many former students say the school taught them to be independent and to plan their own time. Ellie agrees. “I love my school,” she says. “And I'm never late for class. My classroom is only twenty steps from my bedroom!”
